patterns.reason: The other 14,651 German members were assigned solely through a candidate-index match of the short sequence gen. Common unrelated endings in erfolgen, sorgen, bestätigen, entscheidungen and thousands more do not establish descent from Greek genea. Preserve the three specified members; keep other languages' members untouched.
The remaining strings include personal names and brands (Imogene, Genevan, Genetix), unrelated -gene compounds, malformed tokens and compound-only links such as genepool.

Spanish génesis and its compounds derive from Greek genesis, not genea; gene and other residual strings are foreign tokens, names, brands or unsupported substring matches. The Spanish word gen is not present among this family's members.

Italian genio/genia derive from Latin genius, -geni formations have other immediate etymons, and the rest are names, fragments or accidental strings. No direct genea member is demonstrated in this list.

English sound (auditory sense) descends through Old French son from sonus; sonnet and its plural/derivative descend through Occitan sonet. Son 'child', net/network, planet, surnames and unrelated internal strings do not belong to the same family. The source label manually_verified on a morphological candidate is not an individual etymological review.

French sonnet has the sound/song etymology. Unqualified son and sons are sense-ambiguous with possessive and other homonyms in this sense-free corpus, while the other entries mostly match surnames or incidental son strings.
Spanish sónico is the sound-related adjective. Bare son is ambiguous with the verb ser, and the list is dominated by -son surnames, names, foreign strings and unsupported matches.
Italian suono and its clipped form suon descend from sonus; sonetto follows Old Occitan sonet. The other three are unsupported surface strings.

Delete this incoherent association family while preserving the lemmas and their other family memberships.
